commands: kubectl get pods -n test-social-network; kubectl get events -n test-social-network --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -20

cd /tmp; kubectl get svc,ep -n test-social-network | awk '{print $1,$2,$3,$5}' | head -80; kubectl get deploy -n test-social-network -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image} {.spec.template.spec.containers[0].ports[*].containerPort}{"\n"}{end}'

kubectl get svc post-storage-service media-frontend -n test-social-network -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.ports}{"\n"}{end}'; kubectl get deploy media-frontend -n test-social-network -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].ports}'

kubectl patch svc post-storage-service -n test-social-network --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":9090}]'; kubectl get ep post-storage-service -n test-social-network
agent.summary:
I found one fault and fixed it: the `post-storage-service` Service had `targetPort: 9999`, but the pod listens on 9090.

All pods were Running with no restarts, but that mismatch meant callers couldn't reach post-storage. That would break reading and writing posts, and the timeline reads that depend on them.

I patched the Service to `targetPort: 9090`. Its endpoint is now `10.244.1.65:9090`. I haven't run a post or timeline request against the service, so the fix is confirmed only by the endpoint change.

`media-frontend` has a similar-looking mapping (Service targetPort 8080, container port 8081). I left it alone because I believe it matches the stock DeathStarBench setup, though I didn't check that against a reference.
